Main.sentence: A presidential memorandum (from Latin memorare , 'to remember') is a type of ___E:directive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_directive)___ issued by the ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ to manage and govern the actions, practices, and policies of the various departments and agencies found under the ___E:executive branch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_branch)___ of the ___E:United States government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_government)___ .
It has the force of law and is usually used to delegate tasks, direct specific government agencies to do something, or to start a regulatory process.
There are three types of presidential memoranda: presidential determination or presidential finding, memorandum of disapproval, and hortatory memorandum.

Sometimes used interchangeably, an ___E:executive order U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_order_(United_States))___ is a more prestigious form of executive action that must cite the specific ___E:constitutional U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Constitution)___ or statutory authority the president has to use it.  Unlike executive orders, memoranda are not required by law to be published in the Federal Register , but publication is necessary in order to have "general applicability and legal effect".
The Federal Register gives publication priority to executive orders and ___E:presidential proclamations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_proclamations)___ over memoranda.
Memoranda can be amended or rescinded by executive orders or another memorandum, but executive orders take legal precedence and cannot be changed by a memorandum.
In the past, presidential memoranda have been referred to as presidential letters .

___E:Presidential determination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_determination)___ , or presidential finding, are memoranda required by a ___E:statute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statute)___ and must be issued before certain actions are taken.
For example, a presidential determination on the status of a country must be released before sanctions are imposed on the country.
A memorandum of disapproval is a public veto statement.

A hortatory memorandum is issued as a broad policy statement, but unlike a ___E:presidential proclamation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Proclamation)___ is directed to executive agencies.

In 2017, President ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ issued the ___E:national security directives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_security_directive)___ under the name of "national security presidential memorandums".

They operate like ___E:executive orders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_order_(United_States))___ , but are only in the area of ___E:national security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_security_of_the_United_States)___ .
They date back to President ___E:Harry S. Truman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S._Truman)___ and have been issued by various presidents under different names.
